hook_text: One cell: dim orange. Two: yellow. Three: bright white. Then add resistors and watch it fade. That is Ohm's law, and you can see it with your eyes.
clip_script: Three quantities: volts are the push, amps are the flow, ohms are the squeeze. Like a water tank, a pipe and a kink, except charge never leaks, so current is the same all round the loop. Fair test one: add cells in series, same lamp; more push, more flow, brighter, though not quite doubling because the hot filament resists more, and you write that down honestly. Fair test two: same cells, add resistors; more squeeze, less flow, dimmer. Ohm's law in words, both ways. Ammeter in the loop, voltmeter across a part, and never the ammeter across a cell.
visual_style: Whiteboard circuit with a lamp brightening as cells stack; a results table filling in; resistors slotting in as the lamp fades; a tank-pipe-kink sketch; meter connection diagrams.
pacing: Three quantities, analogy, test one, test two, law and limits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the three-cell test with a results table.
